summary: The testing component is the evidence-producing verify stage of the loop. The VerificationGate runs an ordered set of language-aware checks (syntax, format, lint, typecheck, test, security) over the project after edits, grading the result against a QaProfile and QaWeights into a QualityGrade and VerificationReport. VisualVerifier and VisualStateTracker verify UI screenshots against expectations and detect stuck visual loops. It gates the act->learn transition: work is only accepted as done when the VerificationReport passes, reshaping the loop into a verify-then-commit cycle.
context_basis: Recommendations were formed reading src/testing/ (verification VerificationGate, qa_profiles, visual_verification, language_qa) in the context of the full engine at a ~600k budget framing, where the gate replaces inline post-edit verification in the act stage.

examples.title: Gate the act with a verification pass
examples.intent: Only mark work done when the VerificationGate reports success.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Inserts a VerificationGate.run after edits; a failing VerificationReport keeps the loop iterating instead of transitioning to Completed.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw an edge from the act node into the verification gate before the loop can reach Completed.
touch_interaction.visual: The gate renders as a checklist card; it pulses while running, then stamps a green PASS or red FAIL.

examples.mini_scenario: The agent edits code and the gate runs; the VerificationReport fails on a type error, so the loop reasons about a fix rather than finishing.
examples.pitfall: Never accept completion without a passing report; a skipped gate lets broken edits count as done.

examples.title: Detect repo language to pick checks
examples.intent: Run the right toolchain checks for the project's language.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: RepoLanguage detection (from_extension/from_manifest) selects a LanguageCheckSet so the verify stage uses the correct linters and compilers.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the gate to see the detected language and the check set it will run.
touch_interaction.visual: A language badge (Rust/Python/TS/Go) appears with the enabled check icons beneath it.

examples.mini_scenario: A Cargo.toml is present; from_manifest detects Rust and the gate wires in cargo check, clippy, and fmt.
examples.pitfall: Mixed-language repos need a hint; relying on one manifest can miss checks for a secondary language.

examples.title: Order QA stages syntax-to-security
examples.intent: Run cheap checks before expensive ones and fail fast.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: QaStage order (Syntax, Format, Lint, TypeCheck, Test, Security) lets the gate short-circuit early, saving loop budget on obviously broken edits.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread the gate to fan the stages into an ordered pipeline of chips.
touch_interaction.visual: Stages light green left-to-right; a failing stage turns red and halts the ones downstream.

examples.mini_scenario: A syntax error fails the first stage, so the gate never spends time running the full test suite.
examples.pitfall: Keep the cheap-to-expensive order; running Test before Syntax wastes budget on unparseable code.

examples.title: Grade the run against a QaProfile
examples.intent: Convert stage results into a single QualityGrade.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: compute_score applies QaWeights to QaStageResults; QualityGrade.from_score decides whether the loop's output meets the bar.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch the gate to collapse per-stage detail into a single letter grade.
touch_interaction.visual: A grade medallion (A-F) with a weighted score ring; passing grades glow gold.

examples.mini_scenario: Lint and test pass but security is weak; the weighted score lands a B, which the strict profile rejects.
examples.pitfall: Match the profile to the task; a minimal profile can grade risky code as passing by under-weighting security.

examples.title: Choose fast vs thorough config
examples.intent: Trade verification depth against loop budget.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VerificationConfig::fast or ::thorough sets how many checks run, scaling the verify stage's cost per iteration.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotate the gate's depth dial between Fast and Thorough.
touch_interaction.visual: Fast shows a lean two-stage strip; Thorough expands to the full six-stage pipeline.

examples.mini_scenario: Mid-loop with tight budget, the gate runs the fast config (syntax+lint only), deferring full tests to the final iteration.
examples.pitfall: Do not ship on fast alone; a final thorough pass must run before declaring the task complete.

examples.title: Report errors with severity
examples.intent: Distinguish blocking errors from warnings in the report.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VerificationError with ErrorSeverity lets the loop treat warnings as non-blocking while errors force another iteration.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the report to expand errors grouped by severity.
touch_interaction.visual: Errors render red, warnings amber; a count badge per severity sits on the report card.

examples.mini_scenario: A lint pass yields warnings but no errors; the gate lets the loop proceed while surfacing the warnings.
examples.pitfall: Do not block on every warning; treating advisory lint as fatal stalls the loop on non-issues.

examples.title: Run a custom post-edit test command
examples.intent: Verify with the project's own test command after edits.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: set_post_edit_test_command adds a CustomCheck the gate runs, tying the verify stage to the repo's real test harness.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the gate to type or edit the post-edit test command.
touch_interaction.visual: A command chip attaches to the gate; it spins while the command runs and colors by exit code.

examples.mini_scenario: The gate runs npm test after each edit; a failing suite feeds a red CheckResult back into the loop.
examples.pitfall: Scope the command to the changed area when possible; a full slow suite on every edit throttles the loop.

examples.title: Exclude generated files from checks
examples.intent: Skip vendored or generated files that would pollute the report.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: is_excluded filters files out of the check set so the verify stage grades only authored code.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick an excluded file chip off the gate's target list.
touch_interaction.visual: Excluded files gray out with a strike-through; the target count drops.

examples.mini_scenario: A generated protobuf file triggers lint noise; is_excluded drops it so the report reflects only hand-written code.
examples.pitfall: Exclude noise, not real code; over-broad excludes can hide genuine failures from the gate.

examples.title: Track side effects of verification
examples.intent: Know when a check itself mutated the workspace.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: SideEffect/SideEffectType flags that a formatter or fixer changed files, so the loop re-reads state before continuing.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the report to see which checks produced side effects.
touch_interaction.visual: Side-effect checks show a small wrench badge indicating files were modified.

examples.mini_scenario: A format check rewrites files; the SideEffect flag tells the loop to re-perceive the workspace before the next reasoning step.
examples.pitfall: Re-read after side-effecting checks; stale in-context file content diverges from what the formatter wrote.

examples.title: Verify a UI against expectation
examples.intent: Confirm a rendered screen matches the intended UI.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VisualVerifier produces a VisualVerificationResult that gates whether a UI-changing act is accepted.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread on the screenshot node to zoom into verified UI elements.
touch_interaction.visual: Matched elements outline green, missing or wrong ones outline red with a mismatch label.

examples.mini_scenario: After a layout edit, VisualVerifier checks the screenshot; a missing button yields a failing ElementVerification and the loop retries.
examples.pitfall: Verify against a specific expectation, not just 'looks fine'; vague checks pass broken UIs.

examples.title: Diff two UI states visually
examples.intent: Measure what actually changed on screen after an act.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VisualDiffResult quantifies the delta between screenshots, letting the loop confirm the intended visual change occurred.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotate a slider to wipe between the before and after screenshots.
touch_interaction.visual: Changed regions highlight with a colored overlay; the diff percentage shows on the node.

examples.mini_scenario: An edit should recolor a header; the VisualDiffResult confirms the header region changed and nothing else regressed.
examples.pitfall: Ignore trivial pixel noise; a raw diff without tolerance flags anti-aliasing as a real change.

examples.title: Detect a stuck visual loop
examples.intent: Notice the agent repeating the same screen without progress.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VisualStateTracker flags a LoopDetectionResult when screenshots repeat, forcing a RecoveryStrategy instead of endless retries.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the tracker to see the repeated-state count against the stuck threshold.
touch_interaction.visual: Repeated frames stack with a pulsing loop icon; crossing the threshold flashes a break-loop alert.

examples.mini_scenario: The agent keeps clicking a dialog that never closes; matching perceptual hashes trip the stuck threshold and the loop switches tactics.
examples.pitfall: Compare perceptual hashes with a similarity tolerance; exact-match only misses near-identical stuck states.

examples.title: Hash screens to spot repetition
examples.intent: Fingerprint each screen to compare states cheaply.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: compute_perceptual_hash and compute_hash_similarity let the tracker record ScreenshotStates and detect near-duplicates across iterations.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap a frame to see its perceptual hash and similarity to recent frames.
touch_interaction.visual: Each frame shows a compact hash chip; similar frames link with a dotted resemblance line.

examples.mini_scenario: Two consecutive screens hash to near-identical values; has_similar_state returns true, feeding the loop detector.
examples.pitfall: Tune the similarity threshold; too tight over-flags, too loose lets a genuinely stuck loop slip through.

examples.title: Recommend a recovery on visual stall
examples.intent: Pick a way out when the UI is stuck.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A RecoveryStrategy from the visual tracker redirects the loop (e.g. reload, alternate path) instead of repeating the failing action.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the stuck alert to choose from suggested recovery strategies.
touch_interaction.visual: A radial menu of recovery options fans out; the recommended one is pre-highlighted.

examples.mini_scenario: Detecting a stuck modal, the tracker recommends a page reload, breaking the repeated-click cycle.
examples.pitfall: Escalate strategies; repeating the same recovery that already failed just nests one loop inside another.

examples.title: Delegate to language QA runners
examples.intent: Use each language's native QA tools rather than inline heuristics.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: QaLanguage.detect selects the language QA runner so the verify stage invokes real linters/compilers, replacing inline Python/Node/Go checks.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the language QA node to see which runner and tools were selected.
touch_interaction.visual: A toolchain badge lists the invoked binaries (clippy, mypy, eslint, go vet).

examples.mini_scenario: detect finds a Python project; the gate runs mypy and ruff instead of a hand-rolled syntax heuristic.
examples.pitfall: Ensure the toolchain is installed; a missing linter must surface as unavailable, not as a silent pass.

examples.title: Cache last results for quick recheck
examples.intent: Avoid re-running unchanged checks every iteration.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: last_results holds the prior VerificationReport so the loop can re-verify only what changed, cutting verify cost per iteration.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick the gate to re-run only the checks touching changed files.
touch_interaction.visual: Unchanged stages stay dimmed with cached green; only affected stages re-animate.

examples.mini_scenario: One file changed; the gate reuses last_results for untouched checks and only reruns the affected stage.
examples.pitfall: Invalidate the cache on config or dependency changes; a cross-cutting change can invalidate all cached stages.

examples.title: Analyze layout beyond pixels
examples.intent: Verify UI structure and alignment, not just color.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: LayoutAnalysis inspects element arrangement so the gate can reject structurally broken UIs that a color diff would miss.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread to overlay a layout grid on the screenshot with detected UiElements.
touch_interaction.visual: Elements snap to bounding boxes; misaligned ones flag with a red guide line.

examples.mini_scenario: A button overlaps a field; LayoutAnalysis flags the collision even though colors matched, so the gate rejects.
examples.pitfall: Combine structural and pixel checks; either alone misses a class of UI regressions.

examples.title: Mock external APIs during verification
examples.intent: Make tests deterministic by stubbing network dependencies.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: mock_api provides stubbed responses so the verify stage does not depend on flaky external services, stabilizing the loop's pass/fail signal.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the gate to attach a mock API profile for the test run.
touch_interaction.visual: A mock badge attaches; outbound network edges reroute to a stub node.

examples.mini_scenario: A test hitting a payment API uses mock_api stubs, so the verify result reflects code correctness, not upstream availability.
examples.pitfall: Keep mocks faithful to the real contract; a stale stub can pass code that breaks against the live API.

examples.title: Feed the report into the learn stage
examples.intent: Turn a verification outcome into durable evidence.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The VerificationReport becomes Evidence the learn stage records, so future loops know which checks a change must satisfy.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick a passed report into the memory node to record it as evidence.
touch_interaction.visual: The report card animates into memory and leaves a small verified-evidence marker.

examples.mini_scenario: A passing report is stored as evidence; a later regression can be traced to the check that once passed.
examples.pitfall: Record the grade and the failing checks, not just pass/fail; the detail is what makes the evidence useful later.

examples.title: Compose the verify stage as one gate
examples.intent: Fuse language checks, QA grading, and visual verification into one gate node.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Chains RepoLanguage detection -> staged QA pipeline -> QualityGrade -> optional VisualVerifier so one gate decides accept/iterate for every act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch to collapse the verification sub-nodes into one gate chip on the act->done edge.
touch_interaction.visual: Collapsed it shows a checkmark with the current grade; spread reveals the language, QA pipeline, grade, and visual sub-nodes.

examples.mini_scenario: An edit flows through language detection, the six QA stages, a B+ grade, and a visual check; all pass, so the gate accepts and records evidence.
examples.pitfall: Order it correctly: detect language, run cheap-to-expensive stages, grade, then visual-verify, and always emit a report even on early failure.
